title: A Causal Framework for GaN Power HEMT Reliability: Degradation Mechanisms, Indicators, Mitigation and Lifetime Modelling
content: Gallium nitride (GaN) high-electron-mobility transistors enable power converters switching in the megahertz range, but their reliability is governed by mechanisms that differ from those of silicon carbide (SiC) MOSFETs. This review organises the evidence in a four-stage causal chain (stressor, mechanism, state change, failure mode), with indicators and mitigation treated as overlays. The chain separates reversible trap filling from irreversible defect generation, which alone accumulates over a service life. Applied to more than 200 sources, it yields four findings. First, dynamic on-state resistance, the most widely reported GaN-specific indicator, is not monotonic in stress, so monitoring requires at least two indicators of different provenance. Second, the lateral geometry moves the package failure site to the solder: wire-bonded lateral devices have survived several million power cycles, whereas chip-scale solder joints fail after hundreds to thousands of thermal cycles. Third, published lifetime projections for GaN converters range from tens to about 10¹⁰ years, depend strongly on the end-of-life criterion and have not been validated independently. Fourth, standards define how to measure dynamic on-state resistance but set no acceptance criterion. Finally, an experimental agenda pairs each open question with the experiment that would settle it and the outcome that present evidence predicts.
